predecessors.name: Republic of China
predecessors.text: 'the military governor of Fengtian' (Liaoning), seized in 1916 from Duan Zhigui

successors.name: Manchukuo
successors.text: Manchuria, overrun by the Japanese Kwantung Army from 18 September 1931 and turned into Manchukuo (1 March 1932)

ledger.x: 1916: Zhang Zuolin seizes Fengtian.
1918: Zhang's control of Manchuria is complete.
April 1922: the First Zhili-Fengtian War.
18 June 1922: Zhili victory; the peace was 'signed on June 18, 1922, aboard a British warship off Qinhuangdao'.
15 September 1924: the Second Zhili-Fengtian War begins (infobox 'September 15, 1924 - November 3, 1924'); the prelude was the First Jiangsu-Zhejiang War of 3 September 1924.
3 November 1924: Wu Peifu leaves Tianjin by sea and the war is over: 'Anti-Zhili alliance victory'.
November 1924: Zhili's north falls.
November 1924 (bridging): Rehe, Zhili's since June 1922 (zhili-clique /ledger/4), is taken in the same collapse of 'all of its northern provinces to Zhang Zuolin and Feng Yuxiang's Guominjun'.
By August 1925: Shandong is Fengtian's.
By August 1925: Jiangsu and Anhui are Fengtian's.
25 November 1925: Jiangsu (and with it Anhui) pass back to Sun Chuanfang.
June 1926: Zhang captures Beijing.
18 June 1927: Zhang Zuolin proclaims himself Generalissimo of the Military Government of the Republic of China.
30 April 1928: the National Revolutionary Army enters Jinan ('the NRA entered Jinan on 30 April 1928'); the Jinan incident with Japan followed on 8 May.
June 1928: Zhang withdraws and dies.
29 December 1928: Manchuria joins the Nationalist flag.

December 1929 (bridging): the Cliopatria row changes from Kuomintang to Republic of China and the Nationalist government of Nanjing continues under the second name, so the relation is closed here and reopened with republic-of-china the next line; the Northern Expedition page is silent on 1929, so the year is a reading.
1930 (bridging): Zhang Xueliang's Manchuria continues as a quasi-independent ally of the Nanjing government, now under the Republic of China row.
September 1930: the Northeast Army enters North China.
18 September 1931: the Mukden Incident.
18 September 1931: the Mukden Incident and the invasion end the relation in fact: the invasion began 'on 18 September 1931, immediately following the Mukden Incident'; Zhang's armies did not resist.
February 1932: Manchuria is lost.
February 1932 (bridging, placed at the dissolve): the Northeast Army's North China holdings leave the dossier with the state.
February 1932: the Fengtian clique's Manchuria passes to Japan's puppet state.

wars.name: First Zhili-Fengtian War
wars.outcome: Zhili victory: Fengtian defeated on 4 May 1922 and retired to Manchuria; peace signed 18 June 1922; Shanhaiguan became the border.

wars.name: Second Zhili-Fengtian War
wars.outcome: Anti-Zhili alliance victory: Feng Yuxiang's coup of 22 October and the Fengtian advance ended Zhili control of the north; Duan Qirui's provisional government followed and Shandong went to Zhang.

wars.name: Guo Songling rebellion
wars.outcome: Zhang Zuolin put down the revolt: 'Guo ... rebelled in November 1925' (Fengtian page) and 'Zhang managed to put down the revolt in December' (Zhang page).

wars.name: Anti-Fengtian War
wars.outcome: Fengtian and Zhili victory (infobox): Guo Songling's siege of Mukden, begun on 22 November 1925, was lifted and he was killed on 24 December 1925; 'In December 1925, Feng Yuxiang of the Guominjun temporarily seized the city of Tianjin from Li Jinglin'; in…

wars.name: Northern Expedition
wars.outcome: Kuomintang victory: Jinan on 30 April 1928, Beijing on 6 June, Tianjin on 11 June; the Beiyang government ended and Zhang Xueliang declared allegiance to Nanjing on 29 December 1928.

wars.name: Central Plains War
wars.outcome: Nationalist victory after Zhang Xueliang's Northeast Army entered the North China Plain in September 1930; Yan and Feng resigned on 4 November 1930.

wars.name: Japanese invasion of Manchuria
wars.outcome: Japanese victory: Manchuria seized by the Kwantung Army and Manchukuo established as a puppet state.

certainty.note: Provincial lines in Manchuria; Shanhaiguan was the border with Zhili after 1922.
Control of Zhili, Shandong, Jiangsu and Anhui was military occupation, not a fixed boundary, and shifted between 1925 and 1926.
Manchuria's provincial lines; the Peking corridor of 1930 has no extent on the pages opened.
